The 2026 AI Trust Framework

In an enterprise landscape defined by rapid regulatory shiftsâ€”most notably the full enforcement of the EU AI Act and the adoption of ISO/IEC 42001â€”the AI Trust Index serves as an independent benchmark. We do not accept payment for rankings. Our evaluations are based on a 24-point technical scoring system designed for CTOs, CISOs, and Data Protection Officers.

1. Automated Evidence Integrity (40% Weight)

We evaluate the "API Depth" of each platform. High-scoring platforms must demonstrate the ability to pull raw metadata directly from model weights, training datasets, and CI/CD pipelines without manual intervention. We prioritize platforms that generate immutable audit logs capable of withstanding forensic scrutiny during a "Big 4" audit.

2. Regulatory Control Mapping (30% Weight)

Platforms are tested on their native support for specific AI-risk frameworks. This includes Annex IV technical documentation for the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (RMF), and SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria for AI. A platform that merely offers a generic checklist is penalized; we prioritize those with dynamic, cross-framework control mapping.

3. Real-time Model Monitoring (20% Weight)

Static compliance is no longer sufficient for AI systems. Our methodology rewards platforms that offer continuous, real-time monitoring. If a model's performance drifts, a training set is compromised, or an LLM produces unauthorized output, the compliance platform must trigger an immediate technical alert within the governance dashboard.

4. Audit Ecosystem & Human Support (10% Weight)

We assess the "human bridge" between software and certification. This includes the quality of the partner auditor network (CPAs and IRCA auditors) and the platform's ability to facilitate a seamless "Remote Audit" session through direct evidence access for third-party evaluators.

Note: Our data is refreshed quarterly. As the AI Standards Body issues new harmonized standards, we update our scoring weights to ensure the AI Trust Index remains the definitive technical authority for AI governance.
